bracketing: Source: 2024-25 Principles and Procedures (latest published full version). NCAA says 'existing principles and procedures' carry over to the 76-team bracket; the 2026-27 document had not been published as of this research.

Seed list: committee ranks every team in 'true seed' order (S-curve); seed lines are 4 teams each and should be as equal as possible. No. 1 seeds placed first (Final Four pairings overall 1 vs 4, 2 vs 3); overall No. 1 picks its preferred first/second-round site and region; then 2, 3, 4 lines placed in true-seed order. The committee may relax geography on the 2 line to avoid e.g. overall #5 landing in overall #1's region.
Region balance check after the top 4 lines: sum of true seeds per region; generally no more than 5 points between the highest and lowest region total.
Pods: bracket groups (1,16,8,9), (4,13,5,12), (2,15,7,10), (3,14,6,11) go to the same first/second-round site; two pods per site, which may feed different regions.

Conference separation 1: the first four teams selected from a conference must be in different regions if they are seeded on the top four lines (relaxed if a conference has 5+ teams on the top four lines).
Conference separation 2: same-conference teams that played 3+ times (regular season + conference tournament) cannot meet before the regional final (Elite Eight).
Conference separation 3: same-conference teams that played exactly twice cannot meet before the regional semifinal (Sweet 16), i.e. not in round of 64 or round of 32.
Conference separation 4: same-conference teams that played once or not at all may meet as early as the second round (round of 32) - not in the first round (round of 64).

The three meeting-round rules may be relaxed if a league has 9+ teams in the tournament; any principle can be relaxed if 2+ teams from the same conference are among the last at-large teams in the play-in. For 2027 NCAA says it will also avoid same-conference matchups in the Opening Round and round of 64 where possible.
Seed-line moves: a team may be moved up or down one line from its true seed line (two lines in extraordinary circumstances) to satisfy the principles; the seed list itself is not changed.

Geography: teams stay as close to their natural area as possible (mileage campus-to-venue); higher true seed wins ties for a natural region. Top-4-line teams are not placed at a 'home-crowd disadvantage' in the first round. A team cannot play in a facility where it played more than 3 games that season (excl. exhibitions and conference tournaments), and a host institution cannot play at its own site.

Rematch avoidance (no seed-line moves for this): avoid non-conference regular-season rematches in the play-in and first round (secondary: second round), and rematches from the previous year's tournament in the play-in/first round.

Play-in winners get priority to the closest first-round site from the play-in site; if the top No. 1 seeds would all naturally be Thursday/Saturday, the fourth No. 1 goes to its closest Friday/Sunday site so a Wednesday play-in 16 can play it Friday (likely generalised for 2027 because all four 16 lines come from Opening Round games).
